GraphNodeService（C++）

Service introduction

GraphNodeService is a service Atom SDK dedicated to operating "subgraph nodes (GraphNode) internal subgraphs". GraphNode is a special node type that contains a complete subgraph (nested graph) inside it. Through GraphNodeService, you can open the internal subgraph of GraphNode and perform operations on the nodes that completely correspond to NodeService - including node addition and deletion, port connection, parameter reading and writing, data reading, and subgraph operation.

Header file:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
// or quoted individually(Pass client.hpp automatically included)
#include "atom_sdk/services/graph_node.hpp"

Entrance:

atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
atom::sdk::GraphNodeService& gns = client.graph_node();

Applicable scenarios

  • Build a multi-layer nested complex graph structure (the main graph contains GraphNode, GraphNode contains subgraphs)

  • Perform refined parameter configuration on the internal nodes of the subgraph

  • Read the port data of the internal nodes of the subgraph (including the raw bytes of the point cloud)

  • Run an internal subgraph of GraphNode independently

Main picture vs Sub-picture relationship description

Main picture(Main Graph)
├── Ordinary node A          ← by NodeService management
├── Ordinary node B          ← by NodeService management
└── GraphNode C        ← by NodeService management(as a normal node)
    └── Internal subgraph        ← by GraphNodeService management
        ├── child node C1
        ├── child node C2
        └── child node C3

In the GraphNodeService method, all parameters requiring graph_node_id refer to ID of the GraphNode node in the main graph.

Recommended calling order

client.graph().open_graph(graph_name)
           ↓
 (Create in main image GraphNode,get graph_node_id)
           ↓
    open_graph(graph_name, graph_node_id)   ← Open subplot
           ↓
       create_node                          ← Add nodes to subgraph
           ↓
  set_node_param_data                       ← Set subgraph node parameters
           ↓
      connect_nodes                         ← Connect subgraph node ports
           ↓
       initial_node / activate_node         ← Initialization and activation
           ↓
       run_graph                            ← Run subgraph
           ↓
   get_node_port_data                       ← Read subgraph node output

Interface detailed explanation

open_graph

JsonObject open_graph(const SubGraphRef& params) const;

Purpose: Open the internal sub-picture of a certain GraphNode in the main picture and enter the editing state.

parameters type Description

graph_name

std::string

Main image name

graph_node_id

std::string

ID of the GraphNode node in the main graph

*Return value: * JsonObject, containing subgraph status information.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");

    // Open the main image first
    client.graph().open_graph("main_graph");

    // open GraphNode internal subgraph of
    auto result = client.graph_node().open_graph({"main_graph", "graph_node_001"});

    std::cout << "Subpicture is open,Can start editing" << std::endl;

    return 0;
}

edit_graph_name

JsonValue edit_graph_name(const EditSubGraphNameParams& params) const;

Use: Modify the name of the GraphNode internal subgraph.

Example:

client.graph_node().edit_graph_name(
    {"main_graph", "graph_node_001", "subgraph_v2"});

get_all_nodes_info

JsonObject get_all_nodes_info() const;

Purpose: Read all node definitions available in subgraph editing scenarios. The returned content is not bound to a certain picture or a certain GraphNode, so no request parameters are required.

Example:

auto nodes = client.graph_node().get_all_nodes_info();

get_graph_bindings

JsonObject get_graph_bindings(const SubGraphRef& params) const;

Purpose: Read the binding information of the subgraph currently exposed to the outside world, often used to confirm which subgraph input and output can be accessed in the Runtime stage.

Example:

auto bindings = client.graph_node().get_graph_bindings(
    {"main_graph", "graph_node_001"});

get_graph_dl_nodes_model_info

JsonObject get_graph_dl_nodes_model_info(const SubGraphRef& params) const;

Purpose: Read the model information that the deep learning node in the subgraph depends on, usually called before exporting the subgraph.

Example:

auto dl_models = client.graph_node().get_graph_dl_nodes_model_info(
    {"main_graph", "graph_node_001"});

get_graph_custom_nodes

JsonObject get_graph_custom_nodes(const SubGraphRef& params) const;

Purpose: Read the custom node information referenced in the subgraph, usually called before exporting the subgraph.

Example:

auto custom_nodes = client.graph_node().get_graph_custom_nodes(
    {"main_graph", "graph_node_001"});

set_subgraph_as_custom_subgraph

JsonObject set_subgraph_as_custom_subgraph(
    const SetSubgraphAsCustomSubgraphParams& params) const;

Purpose: Save the current GraphNode internal sub-picture as a custom sub-picture template for subsequent reuse in other pictures.

Example:

client.graph_node().set_subgraph_as_custom_subgraph(
    {"main_graph", "graph_node_001", "custom_subgraph"});

create_node

JsonObject create_node(const SubGraphCreateNodeParams& params) const;

Use: Create a new node in the internal subgraph of GraphNode.

parameters type Description

graph_name

std::string

Main image name

graph_node_id

std::string

GraphNode node ID

node_name

std::string

The name of the node type to create

*Return value: * JsonObject, containing new node information:

field type Description

nodeId

string

The unique ID of the new node in the subgraph

name

string

Node type name

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
    client.graph().open_graph("main_graph");
    client.graph_node().open_graph({"main_graph", "graph_node_001"});

    // Create nodes in subgraph
    auto result = client.graph_node().create_node(
        {"main_graph", "graph_node_001", "SegmentationNode"});

    std::string sub_node_id = result.at("nodeId").get<std::string>();
    std::cout << "subgraph node ID:" << sub_node_id << std::endl;
    std::cout << "Request status:" << result.at("status").get<std::int64_t>() << std::endl;

    return 0;
}

create_dynamic_io_node

JsonObject create_dynamic_io_node(
    const CreateDynamicSubGraphNodeParams& params) const;

Use: Create a node with dynamic input and output definitions in the GraphNode internal subgraph.

parameters type Description

graph_name

std::string

Main image name

graph_node_id

std::string

GraphNode node ID

node_name

std::string

The name of the node type to create

node_data

JsonObject

Dynamic input and output definition

Example:

auto inner = client.graph_node().create_dynamic_io_node({
    "main_graph",
    "graph_node_001",
    "DynamicNode",
    atom::sdk::json::parse(R"({"outputs":[{"name":"mask_out"}]})")
});

change_node_io

JsonObject change_node_io(const ChangeSubGraphNodeIOParams& params) const;

Purpose: Modify the input and output structure of dynamic nodes in the subgraph. It is suitable for scenarios where dynamic nodes are created first and then ports are added or adjusted according to business configuration.

Example:

client.graph_node().change_node_io({
    "main_graph",
    "graph_node_001",
    "inner_node_id",
    atom::sdk::json::parse(R"({"inputs":[{"name":"prompt"}]})")
});

create_node_by_copy

JsonObject create_node_by_copy(const SubGraphCopyNodeParams& params) const;

Purpose: Use the existing node in the subgraph as a template to copy a new node of the same type.

parameters type Description

graph_name

std::string

Main image name

graph_node_id

std::string

GraphNode node ID

node_name

std::string

Node type name

node_id

std::string

The node in the copied subgraph ID

*Return value: * JsonObject, contains new node information, the structure is the same as create_node.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
    client.graph().open_graph("main_graph");
    client.graph_node().open_graph({"main_graph", "graph_node_001"});

    // Copy nodes within a subgraph
    auto result = client.graph_node().create_node_by_copy(
        "main_graph",
        "graph_node_001",
        "SegmentationNode",
        "sub_node_abc"   // The copied subgraph node ID
    );
    std::cout << "Request status:" << result.at("status").get<std::int64_t>() << std::endl;

    std::string new_id = result.at("nodeId").get<std::string>();
    std::cout << "Copy the subgraph node ID:" << new_id << std::endl;

    return 0;
}

connect_nodes

JsonObject connect_nodes(const SubGraphConnectionParams& params) const;

Use: In the GraphNode internal subgraph, connect the output port of one node to the input port of another node.

parameters type Description

graph_name

std::string

Main image name

graph_node_id

std::string

GraphNode node ID

input_node_id

std::string

Downstream node ID within the subgraph

input_port_name

std::string

Downstream node input port name

output_node_id

std::string

Upstream node ID within the subgraph

output_port_name

std::string

Upstream node output port name

*Return value: * JsonObject, connection result.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
    client.graph().open_graph("main_graph");
    client.graph_node().open_graph({"main_graph", "graph_node_001"});

    auto result = client.graph_node().connect_nodes(
        "main_graph",
        "graph_node_001",
        "sub_seg_node",     // downstream:split node
        "feat_in",          // downstream input port
        "sub_feat_node",    // upstream:Feature extraction node
        "feat_out"          // upstream output port
    );

    std::cout << "Subgraph node connection successful" << std::endl;

    return 0;
}

disconnect_nodes

JsonObject disconnect_nodes(const SubGraphConnectionParams& params) const;

Use: Break the connection between two node ports in the GraphNode internal subgraph.

parameters type Description

graph_name

std::string

Main image name

graph_node_id

std::string

GraphNode node ID

input_node_id

std::string

Downstream node ID within the subgraph

std::string

Downstream node input port name

output_node_id

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
    client.graph().open_graph("main_graph");
    client.graph_node().open_graph({"main_graph", "graph_node_001"});

    client.graph_node().disconnect_nodes(

get_node_params

JsonObject get_node_params(const SubGraphNodeRef& params) const;

Purpose: Read the parameter snapshot of the specified node in the GraphNode internal subgraph.

parameters type Description

graph_name

std::string

Main image name

graph_node_id

std::string

GraphNode node ID

node_id

std::string

Node ID in subgraph

*Return value: * JsonObject, the current values of all parameters of the subgraph node.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
    client.graph().open_graph("main_graph");
    client.graph_node().open_graph({"main_graph", "graph_node_001"});

    auto params = client.graph_node().get_node_params(
        "main_graph", "graph_node_001", "sub_seg_node"
    );

    for (const auto& [key, val] : params) {
        std::cout << "parameters:" << key << std::endl;
    }

    return 0;
}

get_node_info_in_graph

JsonObject get_node_info_in_graph(const SubGraphNodeRef& params) const;

Purpose: Read the complete information of the specified node in the GraphNode internal subgraph, including ports and connection relationships.

parameters type Description

graph_name

std::string

Main image name

graph_node_id

std::string

GraphNode node ID

node_id

std::string

Node ID in subgraph

*Return value: * JsonObject, complete information of the subgraph node.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
    client.graph().open_graph("main_graph");
    client.graph_node().open_graph({"main_graph", "graph_node_001"});

    auto info = client.graph_node().get_node_info_in_graph(
        "main_graph", "graph_node_001", "sub_seg_node"
    );

    if (info.contains("name")) {
        std::cout << "Node name:" << info.at("name").get<std::string>() << std::endl;
    }

    return 0;
}

get_node_port_data

PortDataResult get_node_port_data(const SubGraphPortRef& params) const;

Purpose: Read the output data (JSON and attachments) of the specified node port in the GraphNode internal subgraph.

parameters type Description

graph_name

std::string

Main image name

graph_node_id

std::string

GraphNode node ID

node_id

std::string

Node ID in subgraph

port_name

std::string

Port name

io_type

std::string

port type, usually "output"

Return value: PortDataResult Structure:

field type Description

data

JsonObject JSON data output from

port

attachments

std::unordered_map<std::string, ByteBuffer>

attachment map, key is the attachment name, value is the original byte

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");

    // Read subgraph node port data after running
    auto run_result = client.graph().run_graph("main_graph");
    std::cout << "Request status:" << run_result.at("status").get<std::int64_t>() << std::endl;

    auto port_data = client.graph_node().get_node_port_data(
        "main_graph",
        "graph_node_001",
        "sub_seg_node",
        "seg_result",     // Segmentation result output port
        "output"
    );

    // read JSON result
    const auto& data = port_data.data;
    std::cout << "Number of result fields:" << data.size() << std::endl;

    if (data.contains("masks")) {
        const auto& masks = data.at("masks");
        std::cout << "Number of masks:" << masks.size() << std::endl;
    }

    // Read attachment
    if (port_data.attachments.count("vis") > 0) {
        const auto& vis = port_data.attachments.at("vis");
        std::cout << "Visualization image size:" << vis.size() << " bytes" << std::endl;
    }

    return 0;
}

download_data

JsonObject download_data(const SubGraphPortRef& params) const;

Use: Generate download links for port data for GraphNode internal subgraph nodes. It is suitable for scenarios where the output of the subgraph port is large and the caller wants to download through the link.

parameters type Description

graph_name

std::string

Main image name

graph_node_id

std::string

GraphNode node ID

node_id

std::string

Node ID in subgraph

port_name

std::string

Port name

io_type

std::string

port type, usually "outputs" or "inputs"

Example:

auto download = client.graph_node().download_data(
    {"main_graph", "graph_node_001", "sub_seg_node", "seg_result", "outputs"});

get_points_data_parsed

std::vector<ParsedPointCloud> get_points_data_parsed(
    const SubGraphPortRef& params) const;

Purpose: Directly read and parse the subgraph node point cloud, it is recommended to use it first.

Example:

auto clouds = client.graph_node().get_points_data_parsed(
    "main_graph",
    "graph_node_001",
    "sub_lidar_node",
    "pc_out",
    "output"
);

get_points_data

ByteBuffer get_points_data(const SubGraphPortRef& params) const;

Purpose: Read the raw byte stream of the point cloud class port in the GraphNode internal subgraph.

parameters type Description

graph_name

std::string

Main image name

graph_node_id

std::string

GraphNode node ID

node_id

std::string

Node ID in subgraph

port_name

std::string

Point cloud output port name

io_type

std::string

port type, usually "output"

*Return value: * ByteBuffer (std::vector<uint8_t>), server raw binary data. Note: * The data returned here also has Atom point cloud header information in front of it. * In ordinary scenarios, it is recommended to use the above get_points_data_parsed() first.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <cstring>
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
    auto run_result = client.graph().run_graph("main_graph");
    std::cout << "Request status:" << run_result.at("status").get<std::int64_t>() << std::endl;

    atom::sdk::ByteBuffer raw = client.graph_node().get_points_data(
        "main_graph",
        "graph_node_001",
        "sub_lidar_node",
        "pc_out",
        "output"
    );

    std::cout << "raw bytes: " << raw.size() << std::endl;

    return 0;
}

set_node_param_data (JSON value overload)

JsonObject set_node_param_data(
    const SubGraphNodeParamUpdate& params) const;

Purpose: Writes the JSON value to the parameter of the specified node in the GraphNode internal subgraph.

parameters type Description

graph_name

std::string

Main image name

graph_node_id

std::string

GraphNode node ID

node_id

std::string

Node ID in subgraph

param_name

std::string

Parameter name

param_type

std::string

parameter category, such as "init_params" or "run_params"

value

const JsonValue&

The JSON value to write

*Return value: * JsonObject, operation result.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
    client.graph().open_graph("main_graph");
    client.graph_node().open_graph({"main_graph", "graph_node_001"});

    // Set numerical parameters
    atom::sdk::JsonValue iou_threshold = 0.45;
    client.graph_node().set_node_param_data(
        "main_graph", "graph_node_001", "sub_seg_node",
        "iou_threshold", "init_params",
        iou_threshold
    );

    return 0;
}

set_node_param_data (file path reload)

JsonObject set_node_param_data(
    const SubGraphNodeParamUpdate& params) const;

Purpose: Automatically upload and write local files to the parameters of the specified node in the GraphNode internal subgraph.

parameters type Description

graph_name

std::string

Main image name

graph_node_id

std::string

GraphNode node ID

node_id

std::string

Node ID in subgraph

param_name

std::string

Parameter name

param_type

std::string

parameter category, usually "init_params"

value

const std::filesystem::path&

local file path, SDK automatically reads and uploads

*Return value: * JsonObject, operation result.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <filesystem>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
    client.graph().open_graph("main_graph");
    client.graph_node().open_graph({"main_graph", "graph_node_001"});

    // Upload the model file of the subgraph node
    client.graph_node().set_node_param_data(
        "main_graph", "graph_node_001", "sub_seg_node",
        "model_file", "init_params",
        std::filesystem::path("/models/seg_model.onnx")
    );

    return 0;
}

set_binding_name

JsonObject set_binding_name(const SubGraphBindingUpdate& params) const;

Purpose: Set the external binding name for a port or parameter of a node in the GraphNode internal subgraph.

parameters type Description

graph_name

std::string

Main image name

graph_node_id

std::string

GraphNode node ID

node_id

std::string

Node ID in subgraph

binding_type

std::string

binding type, such as "output" or "init_params"

origin_name

std::string

The original name of the port or parameter

binding_name

std::string

Exposed binding alias

*Return value: * JsonObject, operation result.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
    client.graph().open_graph("main_graph");
    client.graph_node().open_graph({"main_graph", "graph_node_001"});

    // Bind the subgraph node's output port to an externally accessible name
    client.graph_node().set_binding_name(
        "main_graph", "graph_node_001", "sub_seg_node",
        "output",
        "seg_result",     // original port name
        "sub_output"      // bind alias
    );

    return 0;
}

parameters type Description

Main image name

std::string

GraphNode node ID

Node ID in subgraph

Example:

client.graph_node().edit_node_comment(

activate_node

JsonObject activate_node(
    const SubGraphNodeRef& params,
    std::optional<double> timeout_seconds = 30.0) const;

Purpose: Activate the specified node in the GraphNode internal subgraph, bringing it into the ready state. SDK will poll the server for responses until finish is true or exceeds timeout_seconds.

parameters type Description

graph_name

std::string

Main image name

graph_node_id

std::string

GraphNode node ID

node_id

std::string

Node ID in subgraph

timeout_seconds

std::optional<double>

Polling waiting timeout, default is 30.0 seconds; passing std::nullopt means waiting until completion or the server reports an error

*Return value: * JsonObject, activation result.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
    client.graph().open_graph("main_graph");
    client.graph_node().open_graph({"main_graph", "graph_node_001"});

    client.graph_node().initial_node({"main_graph", "graph_node_001", "sub_seg_node"});
    client.graph_node().activate_node(
        {"main_graph", "graph_node_001", "sub_seg_node"}, 60.0);

    return 0;
}

initial_node

JsonObject initial_node(const SubGraphNodeRef& params) const;

Purpose: Initialize the specified node in the GraphNode internal subgraph (load models, allocate resources, etc.). Need to be called after setting all parameters.

parameters type Description

graph_name

std::string

Main image name

graph_node_id

std::string

GraphNode node ID

node_id

std::string

Node ID in subgraph

*Return value: * JsonObject, initialization result.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <filesystem>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
    client.graph().open_graph("main_graph");
    client.graph_node().open_graph({"main_graph", "graph_node_001"});

    // Set model parameters
    client.graph_node().set_node_param_data(
        "main_graph", "graph_node_001", "sub_seg_node",
        "model_file", "init_params",
        std::filesystem::path("/models/seg_model.onnx")
    );

    // initialization(Trigger model loading)
    client.graph_node().initial_node(
        "main_graph", "graph_node_001", "sub_seg_node"
    );

    return 0;
}

update_node

JsonObject update_node(const SubGraphNodeRef& params) const;

Purpose: Updates the configuration of the specified node in the GraphNode internal subgraph, triggering a recalculation. This interface only initiates one request as defined by the server UpdateNode and does not poll finish; if the server returns finish=false, SDK will also return this response directly to the caller.

parameters type Description

graph_name

std::string

Main image name

graph_node_id

std::string

GraphNode node ID

node_id

std::string

Node ID in subgraph

*Return value: * JsonObject, update result.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
    client.graph().open_graph("main_graph");
    client.graph_node().open_graph({"main_graph", "graph_node_001"});

    // Update after modifying parameters
    atom::sdk::JsonValue new_val = 0.6;
    client.graph_node().set_node_param_data(
        "main_graph", "graph_node_001", "sub_seg_node",
        "iou_threshold", "run_params", new_val
    );
    client.graph_node().update_node(
        "main_graph", "graph_node_001", "sub_seg_node"
    );

    return 0;
}

export_graph

JsonObject export_graph(const ExportSubGraphParams& params) const;

Purpose: Export GraphNode internal subgraph, which can be accompanied by deep learning model information and custom node information that the subgraph depends on.

Example:

auto dl_models = client.graph_node().get_graph_dl_nodes_model_info(
    {"main_graph", "graph_node_001"});
auto custom_nodes = client.graph_node().get_graph_custom_nodes(
    {"main_graph", "graph_node_001"});

auto exported = client.graph_node().export_graph(
    {"main_graph", "graph_node_001", dl_models, custom_nodes});

release_graph

JsonValue release_graph(const SubGraphRef& params) const;

Purpose: Release the editing resources of the GraphNode internal subgraph. If you want to continue editing after releasing, you need to call open_graph again.

Example:

client.graph_node().release_graph({"main_graph", "graph_node_001"});

clear_graph

JsonObject clear_graph(const SubGraphRef& params) const;

Purpose: Clean up the running intermediate state of the GraphNode internal subgraph, but retain the subgraph structure and node parameters.

Example:

client.graph_node().clear_graph({"main_graph", "graph_node_001"});

run_graph

JsonObject run_graph(
    const SubGraphRef& params,
    std::optional<double> timeout_seconds = 30.0) const;

Purpose: Run the GraphNode internal subgraph independently, triggering the execution of all nodes in the subgraph in topological order. SDK will poll the server for responses until finish is true or exceeds timeout_seconds.

parameters type Description

graph_name

std::string

Main image name

graph_node_id

std::string

GraphNode node ID

timeout_seconds

std::optional<double>

Polling waiting timeout, default is 30.0 seconds; passing std::nullopt means waiting until completion or the server reports an error

*Return value: * JsonObject, including subgraph running results and status.

Example:

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
    client.graph().open_graph("main_graph");
    client.graph_node().open_graph({"main_graph", "graph_node_001"});

    // Run subgraphs independently,most wait 60 seconds
    auto result = client.graph_node().run_graph(
        {"main_graph", "graph_node_001"}, 60.0);

    if (result.contains("finish")) {
        bool ok = result.at("finish").get<bool>();
        std::cout << "Subgraph execution completed:" << (ok ? "Yes" : "No") << std::endl;
    }
    std::cout << "Request status:" << result.at("status").get<std::int64_t>() << std::endl;

    return 0;
}

Complete example

The following shows a complete process: open GraphNode in the main graph, edit its internal subgraph, run the subgraph and read the results.

#include "atom_sdk/client.hpp"
#include <filesystem>
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    try {
        atom::sdk::AtomClient client("http://127.0.0.1:10026");
        auto& gs   = client.graph();
        auto& ns   = client.node();
        auto& gns  = client.graph_node();

        // 1. Open main image
        gs.open_graph("main_graph");

        // 2. Create in main image GraphNode(Use as a normal node NodeService)
        auto gn = ns.create_node({"main_graph", "GraphNode", "Nested subgraph nodes"});
        std::string graph_node_id = gn.at("nodeId").get<std::string>();
        std::cout << "GraphNode ID：" << graph_node_id << std::endl;

        // 3. open GraphNode internal subgraph of
        gns.open_graph("main_graph", graph_node_id);

        // 4. Create nodes in subgraph
        auto feat_node = gns.create_node(
            "main_graph", graph_node_id,
            "FeatureExtractNode", "Feature extraction"
        );
        std::string feat_id = feat_node.at("nodeId").get<std::string>();

        auto seg_node = gns.create_node(
            "main_graph", graph_node_id,
            "SegmentationNode", "Instance splitting"
        );
        std::string seg_id = seg_node.at("nodeId").get<std::string>();

        // 5. Upload subgraph node model file
        gns.set_node_param_data(
            "main_graph", graph_node_id, seg_id,
            "model_file", "init_params",
            std::filesystem::path("/models/seg_model.onnx")
        );

        // 6. Set subgraph nodes JSON parameters
        atom::sdk::JsonValue iou_thr = 0.45;
        gns.set_node_param_data(
            "main_graph", graph_node_id, seg_id,
            "iou_threshold", "init_params", iou_thr
        );

        // 7. Connect subgraph nodes
        gns.connect_nodes(
            "main_graph", graph_node_id,
            seg_id, "feat_in",
            feat_id, "feat_out"
        );

        // 8. Initialize and activate subgraph nodes
        gns.initial_node({"main_graph", graph_node_id, seg_id});
        gns.activate_node({"main_graph", graph_node_id, seg_id});

        // 9. Run subgraph
        auto run_res = gns.run_graph({"main_graph", graph_node_id});
        std::cout << "Subgraph execution completed,Request status:" << run_res.at("status").get<std::int64_t>() << std::endl;

        // 10. Read subgraph node port data
        auto port_data = gns.get_node_port_data(
            "main_graph", graph_node_id, seg_id,
            "seg_result", "output"
        );
        std::cout << "Number of result fields:" << port_data.data.size() << std::endl;

        for (const auto& [att_name, att_bytes] : port_data.attachments) {
            std::cout << "Accessories [" << att_name << "]:" << att_bytes.size() << " bytes" << std::endl;
        }

    } catch (const atom::sdk::AtomError& e) {
        std::cerr << "SDK Error:" << e.what() << std::endl;
        return 1;
    }

    return 0;
}
